meta.name: Duello Quiz design tokens
meta.direction: Vivid game style (v2): saturated violet brand, pink opponent accent, chunky pressable buttons with a bottom depth edge, one colour per category, rounded Nunito type. Replaces the stock Material 3 baseline of v1.
notes: Source of truth for colours, type, spacing, shapes, depth, elevation and motion.
color.<theme>.scheme keys are named exactly like the parameters of androidx.compose.material3.ColorScheme (lightColorScheme / darkColorScheme). Map them 1:1; dynamic colour stays OFF.
color.<theme>.game keys are custom semantic roles that ColorScheme does not have. Expose them through a CompositionLocal (e.g. LocalGameColors) with the same names.

NEW in 2.0.0 — game.pressable*: face / content / depth colours of the chunky pressable button (components.md §1). The depth colour is the visible bottom edge; it is decorative (no contrast requirement) but always darker than the face in both themes.
NEW in 2.0.0 — game.cardBorder / game.cardDepth: 2dp border and bottom depth edge of white 'game cards' (option card, list cards, panels).
NEW in 2.0.0 — game.correctDepth / wrongDepth / pendingDepth / confidenceNDepth: depth edges of the coloured option and Əminlik states.

NEW in 2.0.0 — color.<theme>.category: 8 named accent slots (violet, blue, teal, green, orange, rose, pink, ocean). Categories are DB rows, so a category carries an accent KEY (proposed API field `accentKey`), never a hex value. Each slot has face (text/icons in onFace), depth and a pale container for small uses (chips, quiz top bar tint). Unknown or missing key: slot = categories[index % 8] in server order. Expose as LocalCategoryColors: Map<String, CategoryColors>.
NEW in 2.0.0 — color.<theme>.gradient: two-stop linear gradients (start, end, angle). Text on a gradient must pass 4.5:1 against BOTH stops (checked in contrast.py).

Category faces, Əminlik 3 and the pressable primary keep white text in both themes: they are saturated mid/dark tones chosen so #FFFFFF passes 4.5:1. Saturated colours are never used as text on dark surfaces; dark-theme text accents use the light tones in scheme.*.

All colours are opaque sRGB hex. Disabled states follow Material 3: content onSurface at 38 %, container onSurface at 12 % (see stateLayer). Pressable buttons in the disabled state lose their depth edge (flat).
Every text pair is checked in design/contrast-report.md (WCAG 2.1). Run design/tools/contrast.py after any colour change.
Units: dp for sizes, sp for font sizes and line heights, ms for durations.

NEW in 2.1.0 (retention: daily challenge, streak, XP, notifications) — game.streak / streakContainer / onStreakContainer: the flame of the streak ('Seriya'). streak is an ICON colour (flame, 3:1 non-text) that also passes 4.5:1 on white cards in light theme; the number next to it uses onStreakContainer on streakContainer or scheme.onSurface. Burnt orange, deliberately not gold/yellow (no casino look) and distinct from game.timerWarning in hue use (timer = time pressure, streak = habit).

NEW in 2.1.0 — gradient.dailyHero (sky blue -> teal, 135 deg): face of the daily challenge card on home and the daily result hero. Distinct from duelHero (violet -> pink) and resultWin (violet -> blue). White text checked against both stops.

NEW in 2.1.0 — size.resultSquare / resultSquareCompact / levelBadge / streakBadgeMinWidth / xpBarHeight / xpBarMiniHeight and motion.progression (XP bar fill, level-up, streak flame, result squares). No other colour roles were added: XP and levels reuse scheme.primary / primaryContainer, the streak freeze reuses scheme.secondary / secondaryContainer, result squares reuse game.correct / game.wrong / scheme.surfaceContainerHighest.

categoryAccentDefaults.notes: Proposed accentKey per seed category (content/backend sets it in the DB row; this table is only the suggestion). Icons stay mapped by icon_key (components.md §5).

stateLayer.notes: Disabled content = onSurface at 0.38, disabled container = onSurface at 0.12 (M3 standard). Disabled text is exempt from WCAG contrast; never use disabled styling for information the user must read. Pressable components do NOT show a ripple: the press is the face moving down onto its depth edge (motion.pressable).

brand.name: Nunito
brand.source: Google Fonts (github.com/google/fonts/ofl/nunito), SIL Open Font License 1.1. Designers: Vernon Adams, Cyreal, Jacques Le Bailly.
brand.delivery: Bundle static TTF instances in res/font (nunito_medium, nunito_semibold, nunito_bold, nunito_extrabold, nunito_black) — or the single variable TTF (wght 200–1000) with FontVariation.weight on API 26+. Do not use downloadable fonts: the first frame and offline start must already use the final font.
brand.coverage: Latin-ext subset covers Azerbaijani: Ə ə Ğ ğ I ı İ i Ö ö Ü ü Ç ç Ş ş. Verified 2026-10-21 by requesting the Google Fonts subset for exactly these glyphs (non-empty glyph kit, unlike an unsupported script) and by rendering the test string in Figma. android-dev re-checks on device with the test string in design/README.md (no fallback glyphs in any weight).
brand.features: Use tabular figures (fontFeatureSettings "tnum") for the timer, progress "3 / 10", score and rating. If a Nunito build lacks tnum, wrap those numbers in a fixed-width box sized for the widest value (e.g. "88") so digits do not jitter.
brand.notWord: Never set text in all caps (Azerbaijani i/İ and ı/I casing, and caps make long words wider).

fallback.name: sans-serif (system: Roboto / Noto Sans)
fallback.notes: Android resolves sans-serif to Roboto with Noto fallback; both cover Azerbaijani Latin.

notes: Names match androidx.compose.material3.Typography parameters.
Sizes are sp so they follow the user's font scale. Every screen must work at font scale 1.3 without truncation and stay usable (scrolling allowed) at 2.0.
Nunito Regular (400) looks thin next to the chunky shapes, so body text uses SemiBold 600 and Medium 500 is the lightest weight (only for long legal/licence text if needed).
Question text uses titleLarge (20sp ExtraBold); options use bodyLarge (16sp SemiBold) so long Azerbaijani words stay narrow. Button labels use labelLarge (16sp ExtraBold).
Width budget: Nunito averages ~0.55 em per lowercase glyph at 600 and ~0.59 em at 800 — about the same as Inter; budgets in copy/az.md were re-checked against labelLarge 16sp.

layout.notes: screenGutter applies below 600dp width; screenGutterWide and centred maxContentWidth at 600dp and above (tablets, landscape). gridGap = gap between category grid cells (both axes).

notes.buttonHeight: Face height of a pressable button; the depth edge (depth.pressable) is added below it, so the total height is 56dp and the touch target stays >= 48dp in the pressed state too.
notes.progressBarHeight: Chunky rounded quiz timer / progress bar (v2: 12dp, was 4dp).
notes.confidenceChip: Minimum face height of an Əminlik tile (duel). Width is one third of the content width minus two space.md gaps (~101dp on a 360dp phone); grows in height at large font scales. A rounded rectangle, never a circle.
notes.categoryTileMinHeight: Grid cell min height on the home screen (2 columns). In the single-column fallback (components.md §5) the min height is 88dp.
notes.duelBadge: Mini Əminlik badge and answer-letter badge in the duel player panel, calibration rows and reveal.
notes.duelPlayerPanelMinHeight: Pinned self/opponent panels in the match header; grows with font scale and in the result phase.
notes.searchPulse: Outer diameter of the decorative search pulse rings around the own avatar on the duel search screen.
notes.resultSquare: Daily result square (correct / wrong / no answer) on the daily result share card: rounded square with a 20dp glyph. resultSquareCompact = the same squares on the home daily card (14dp glyph). Never colour-only: every square carries a check / cross / dash glyph.
notes.levelBadge: Rounded-square level number on the profile level card.
notes.streakBadgeMinWidth: Streak block (flame + number) at the trailing end of the home profile header; also its minimum touch width.
notes.xpBarHeight: XP progress bar on result screens and the profile level card (same chunky look as progressBarHeight). xpBarMiniHeight = home header and profile category rows.

component.dailyCard: extraLarge minus 4 (24dp), like the duel hero card

shape.notes: Names match androidx.compose.material3.Shapes (extraSmall..extraLarge) using RoundedCornerShape(dp). v2 radii are larger (8/12/16/20/28) for the playful look; buttons are rounded rectangles (medium), not pills, so the depth edge reads as a solid block.

depth.notes: The 'chunky' look: a solid edge of the depth colour drawn BELOW the face (same shape, offset down by this many dp). Build it as two stacked shapes (depth shape at y + depth, face on top), not as a blurred shadow. Pressed: the face moves down by the full depth so the edge disappears (motion.pressable). Disabled: no edge. Borders are 2dp (border) on neutral cards and option cards.

component.topAppBar: level0 — no shadow; when content is scrolled under it, a 2dp cardBorder line appears at its bottom
component.card: level0 — solid depth edge (depth.card) instead of a shadow
component.duelOverlayCard: level3 (self-reconnecting overlay card over a scrim)

elevation.notes: v2: depth is shown by the solid bottom edge (see depth), not by blurred shadows or tonal elevation. Real shadows only on floating layers: dialog, snackbar, overlay card.

bouncy.use: Pops: correct option, points pop, result hero, chip lock. Compose spring(dampingRatio = 0.5f, stiffness = 600f).

pressable.haptic: HapticFeedbackType.TextHandleMove (light tick) on press-down for game controls (option card, Əminlik tile, category tile); none for regular buttons.
pressable.notes: On press-down the face translates down by its depth and the depth edge is covered (edge height animates depth -> 0 in sync). The action fires on click (normal release semantics) for every pressable, including game inputs; the animation never delays sending a pick or an answer (DUEL-16). Reduced motion: no translate, the face colour darkens by the pressed state layer instead.

game.quizRevealHoldSource: docs/mvp-spec.md §1 / OQ-023. Server deadline assumes 1500 ms; do not change without a spec change.
game.timerTick: linear, driven by wall-clock (not by animation frames)

timerWarningPulse.repeat: once per remaining second while <= 5 s

optionCorrectPop.notes: Correct card pops once; the check badge scales in 0 -> 1 with the same spring.

categoryGridEnter.notes: Only on first load from network/cache, not on return from a quiz.

duel.notes: Display-only timing for the duel UI. Phase lengths are server rules (docs/mvp-spec.md §2); the client always counts down to the server deadline and never ends or extends a phase on its own. Animations never delay sending a pick or an answer (DUEL-16).

phaseNominalMs.use: Denominator for the timer ring fraction only: fraction = clamp(remaining / nominal, 0, 1).

timerWarningThresholdMs.notes: 0 = no warning colour in that phase. Warning uses game.timerWarning and the existing timerWarningPulse.

phaseTransition.type: body content cross-fade + 1/8 height slide up; the pinned header never moves

confidencePanelEnter.type: panel slides up from the bottom edge + fade

chipPress.notes: Pressable press (motion.pressable) with depth.confidenceChip. round.bet is sent on the tap, before or in parallel with this animation.

revealFlip.rotation: rotationY 0 -> 180 deg, content swaps at 90 deg
revealFlip.notes: Both player panels flip in the SAME frame. Never staggered (fairness).

duel.revealMinRemainingNotes: If round.result arrives with less than this left in the result phase (late message, rejoin), skip flip and count-up and show the final state with a 150 ms cross-fade.

introEnter.type: self row slides in from the start edge, opponent row from the end edge, 1/4 width + fade, same start time

duel.reducedMotion: No pulse, slide, flip, pop, press translate or count-up: content cross-fades in 150 ms and numbers show their final value. Colours, timer ring and all game timing are unchanged.

progression.notes: Display-only motion for XP, levels, streak and the daily result (design/screens/progression.md). Never delays navigation or a request; values shown are always the server's.

xpGainPop.notes: '+70 XP' pops in after the score count-up has started.

xpBarFill.notes: Bar animates from the old to the new fraction. Total for one result <= 1 s (PROG-02).

levelUp.notes: On a level-up the bar fills to 100 %, the level number ticks to the new value, the bar restarts at 0 and fills to the new fraction; the level-up strip expands under it. Multi-level jumps animate once to the final level.

streakIgnite.notes: Outlined flame cross-fades to filled and pops once when streakExtendedToday is shown (result screens) or on the first home frame after the day became active.

resultSquaresEnter.notes: Daily result squares pop in left to right after the score count-up.

progression.countdownTick: Countdown text updates once per second from the server-offset clock; no animation on the digits (tabular figures).
progression.reducedMotion: No pop, ignite, stagger or bar animation: final values at once (bar at its final width, level number final, level-up strip shown without scale). Text and colours identical.

motion.reducedMotion: When the system setting 'Remove animations' (ANIMATOR_DURATION_SCALE = 0) is on: no shake, pulse, pop, slide, press translate or count-up; colour changes and the timer bar still update. Timing of the game (1500 ms reveal) is unchanged.
